record.context_brief: One-dimensional Hessian manifolds from probability families
record.original_question: Can one classify 1-dimensional Hessian manifolds, especially those arising from families of probability distributions such as the statistical manifold of binomial distributions?

evidence.quote: The statistical manifold of binomial distributions is regarded as the standard example of 1-dimensional Hessian manifold (see [4]). Investigate 1-dimensional Hessian manifolds, especially 1-dimensional Hessian manifolds derived from probability distribution families.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Hessian manifold is a triple $(M,\nabla,g)$ consisting of a smooth manifold $M$, a flat affine connection $\nabla$ on $M$, and a Riemannian metric $g$ on $M$ such that, locally around every point, there exist $\nabla$-affine coordinates $(x^1,\dots,x^n)$ and a smooth potential function $\varphi$ with
$$g_{ij} \;=\; \frac{\partial^2 \varphi}{\partial x^i\,\partial x^j}.$$
A standard source of Hessian manifolds is information geometry: given a parametric family of probability distributions $\{p(\,\cdot\,;\theta)\}_{\theta\in\Theta}$, the Fisher information metric on $\Theta$ together with the natural flat connection of an exponential family produces a Hessian structure; for instance, the family of binomial distributions $\mathrm{Bin}(N,\theta)$, $\theta\in(0,1)$, is the canonical example of a 1-dimensional Hessian manifold.

Problem. Classify, up to isomorphism of Hessian manifolds, all connected 1-dimensional Hessian manifolds $(M,\nabla,g)$. In particular, characterize which 1-dimensional Hessian manifolds arise (globally or locally) as statistical manifolds of parametric families of probability distributions, and identify the role of the binomial family within this classification.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: 1-dimensional exponential families on a finite set with constant Hessian sectional curvature have been classified, with binomial families playing the central role. However, a complete classification of all 1-dimensional Hessian manifolds, especially those arising from arbitrary probability distribution families, does not appear to be established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: One-dimensional exponential families with constant Hessian sectional curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of 1-dimensional exponential families on a finite set with constant Hessian sectional curvature; binomial distributions characterize the constant-curvature case.
status_evidence.claim: Partial classification results exist for the constant-curvature subclass, with binomial families as the model case.

status_evidence.title: Locally conformally Hessian and statistical manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Study of statistical and Hessian manifold structures, generalizing the Hessian setting.
status_evidence.claim: General theory of Hessian/statistical manifolds is still actively developed, suggesting full classification in dimension 1 from probability families is not complete.
